item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and routes the replayable body through FilesService.Add without changing Add’s behavior. A alters Add’s buffering and error semantics and bypasses Add from Upload.","reasons":["B implements the exact Upload signature and explicitly rejects an empty filename or nil content before constructing a request.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and forwards the result to s.Add, preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.","A changes every Add call to eagerly read the entire caller-provided body, introducing new memory, timing, streaming, and wrapped-error behavior contrary to preserving Add.","A’s Upload calls a new private add method instead of the required existing FilesService.Add path, creating potential behavioral divergence between the two entry points."],"risks_a":["The Add behavior change is unnecessary scope expansion and can break callers relying on streaming or on source errors occurring during request transmission.","Visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The changelog and README advertise the out-of-contract Add behavior change."],"risks_b":["It adds an unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the requested convenience API.","The multipart test checks field and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.","The retry test counts attempts but does not verify the multipart content on each attempt; validation and source-reader error cases are also untested."]}
